> Tested locally, it works as expected.
> 
> Example code:
> 
> ```gdscript
> func _ready() -> void:
> 	var args := OS.get_cmdline_args()
> 	var session_number := args.find("--session-number")
> 	if session_number >= -1:
> 		var session_number_value := int(args[session_number + 1])
> 		print("Session number: %d" % session_number_value)
> 
> 	var session_count := args.find("--session-count")
> 	if session_count >= -1:
> 		var session_count_value := int(args[session_count + 1])
> 		print("Session count: %d" % session_count_value)
> ```
> 
> Results in the following with 3 instances:
> 
> ```
> Session number: 1
> Session count: 3
> Session number: 2
> Session count: 3
> Session number: 3
> Session count: 3
> ```

By the way, I have checked and this does seem to match correctly with the different debugger console session numbers. So session 1 is actually session 1, 2 is 2, etc. I do remember however this was not assured before and I believe I saw someone mention this in the older threads. I don't know if something has changed but as of now I did not manage to recreate this mismatch, and the session numbers seem to be consistent.

Added the label and acknowledged the args' existence inside `main.cpp`. I had to re-push them to still let them through and not consume them. Let me know if you want me to do it a different way.
I'm still down for making them into getter functions too.
